subtitle: Lesson 25 · Inner Product Spaces, Unitary & Hermitian Operators

code:
a = (2-i, i)   b = (1+i, 3)

term1: (2+i)(1+i) = 1+3i
term2: (-i)(3) = -3i

<a|b> = 1   (purely real)
caption: Everything imaginary cancelled — a real number, confirmed consistent with <b|a> being its own conjugate.

code:
M = [[0,-i],[i,0]]

diagonal real; (-i)* = i matches M_21 -> Hermitian

trace=0, det=-1
lambda^2 - 1 = 0 -> lambda = +/-1   (real)
caption: Hermitian, so its eigenvalues must be real — confirmed: plus and minus one.

code:
N = (1/sqrt2)[[1,i],[i,1]]

N^dagger N = [[1,0],[0,1]] = I   -> unitary

(without 1/sqrt2: N^dagger N = 2I, NOT unitary)
caption: The normalization factor is essential — drop it and the same-looking matrix fails the test entirely.
A clean 50/50 result — equal superposition measured in the standard basis gives an equal chance of each outcome.
